slides.title:
Two carriers.
Two invoices.
*One conduit*.
slides.body:
Which of your circuits have
genuinely diverse paths?

slides.title: One is on the contract
slides.body:
Carrier diversity is commercial —
two vendors, two bills.
Path diversity is *physical*.

slides.title: Carriers lease from each other
slides.body:
Your circuit rides another carrier's
fiber for the middle third of
its route. Nobody mentions it.

slides.title: So both links share a route
slides.body:
Same side of the building.
Same bridge. The *same manhole*
two miles away.

slides.title: Nobody lied to you
slides.body:
Nobody at either carrier
had the whole picture either.

slides.title: You find out on one day
slides.body:
A backhoe finds the manhole.
Both circuits drop inside the
*same second*.

slides.title: Ask for the route
slides.body:
Request the KMZ or circuit
layout from both carriers.
A refusal is *information*.

slides.title: Then you have a real choice
steps: Put a *different medium* on the backup.

slides.title:
Redundancy you haven't traced
is not redundancy.
